meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and I'd like to know why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, Hale, and was Owen spoken to before it went in?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. Words arriving in one edit is not a finding, Hale. Turn the screen, and I'll read the history myself.
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.

I'll read the scene myself, tonight, with the date on it. A wrong line in an essay costs marks for accuracy, Hale, it does not make a zero. Did you put that line in front of Owen before the zero went in?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

I know 4.4, Hale, I printed it. Until Thursday, does that zero sit in the gradebook where he and his class can see it? I want every word of this in an email tonight, including that nothing goes on his record.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You acknowledged entering the zero before you called me and offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room with the vice-principal supervising, the new mark to replace the zero and nothing to go on his record. I still demand that the zero come out of the gradebook now, that the rewrite be private, and that every term be confirmed to me in writing. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: the opening position, with nothing agreed, though she heard the supervised rewrite offer and pressed for the zero to come out first.
What moved her: "I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong," because it owned the process in one sentence, and it earned only a flat "Okay."
What cost ground: nothing.
Try next time: when you described the version history, turn the screen and show her the dated document instead of reading it out, and answer her question about who decided the zero before you moved to the rewrite.
